_note: Config for scripts/ged_cost_benchmark.py, the micro-benchmark behind the GED cost table in docs/adr/0026-break-faithful-metrics-the-implementers-conventions.md. It is a TOOL, not an experiment: it measures how long networkx's optimizer takes on synthetic prediction shapes against the committed fixture gold, which is the evidence for break_metrics.ged.max_nodes_for_optimizer in configs/musique_eval.json. Nothing here scores a system, so there is no experiments/log.md entry. The shapes themselves (their exact step texts and reference patterns) are defined in the script, because a shape IS the measurement's definition and prose cannot state it precisely enough to re-derive; what lives here is which shapes at which sizes are measured, against which gold. timing_budget_seconds is a stop so the tool always terminates: a cell that hits it is printed with a '*' and its seconds are a LOWER BOUND, not a measurement. The seed is threaded for the repo's contract; this tool draws no random numbers, and its output is deterministic apart from wall-clock timings.
_discriminating_pair_note: The last four shapes are a 2x2 added after the PR #45 review, which falsified the ADR's earlier reading of the table: {nonsense label, gold-derived label} x {no reference, one reference}, with label ties held at maximum in all four. The nonsense pair shares its vocabulary and token count and differs only in carrying a reference, and shares no token with either gold, so the four rows together separate three things the earlier shape set confounded - labels tying with each other, labels tying with the GOLD's labels, and the graph carrying edges at all. Read them together with chain_shaped and all_pairs_referencing, which carry edges but distinguishable labels.
